LESSON: FOOD IN OUR ENVIRONMENT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Environment
Topic 1.3: Food in our Environment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Food in our Environment, part of Social Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How is food classified? 2. Why should we observe table manners during meals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify common foods found in the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Food in our Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. classify foods into the three food groups that comprise a balanced meal,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Food in our Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. observe table manners during meals for social wellbeing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Food in our Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. embrace good eating habits to promote good health. • Learners are guided to talk about different foods found in their locality. • Learners with low vision are guided to use digital devices with assistive technology or print materials with appropriate font to search for information on food groups and share in class. Learners with blindness to use digital devices with assistive technology or braille materials to search for the information on food groups and share in class. ● Learners with low vision use pictures cards of common food items or real foods to classify the foods into three groups namely energy giving, body building and protective foods. Learners with blindness are guided to manipulate and use 1. How is food classified? 2. Why should we observe table manners during meals? 7 verb descriptions of common food items and classify the foods into three groups namely energy giving, body building and protective foods. ● Learners are guided to use digital devices with assistive technology, print or braille materials to search for information on table manners and share with peers. ● Learners participate in a demonstration on good table manners then practice them. A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Food in our Environment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
